description: A slow SSD cache no longer freezes or fails running requests during a prefix restore. Before, a request whose cached prefix lived only on the SSD restored it on the inference thread: mx.load() maps the block files lazily, so the real drive read happens inside the next Metal command buffer, and every other request stops decoding for the whole read. When that read takes longer than about 20 s, the macOS GPU watchdog stops the command buffer ('kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout') and the request fails. Now, when the SSD-only part is 256 MB or more, a background thread reads those files once with plain file I/O (no MLX, so no Metal deadlock risk) into the macOS file cache; the request waits like a cache-freshness deferral while running requests keep decoding, then the normal restore reads from RAM. The log shows 'SSD prefetch for <id> done: N blocks, X GB in Ys (Z MB/s)' with the drive's real speed. Measured on a MacBook Pro with the cache on an SD card (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 1.57-1.74 GB SSD-only prefix of 60-67k tokens, cold file cache, 3 runs per arm): off, decode froze 19.9-22.2 s, and the request failed with the GPU watchdog error in the 2 runs where the read took more than 20 s; on, the prefetch read the prefix in 18.5-30.1 s (59-87 MB/s), decode froze 1.6-3.2 s during the restore from RAM, and the request got its full cache hit every time. Limits: while a prefetch runs, no other waiting request is admitted, even when a slot is free (head-of-line wait up to the prefetch time, timeout 600 s); if macOS evicts the file cache before the restore, the old slow read happens; GDN sidecar and boundary snapshot files are not prefetched; the final restore from RAM still pauses other requests for about 1-2 s. OMLX_SSD_PREFETCH=0 turns it off. Built against upstream ade9f20a.
